rows.jp: 扉が開かない。

ghs.en: The door does not open.

rows.jp: 強く押し込むと、目の前に乱気流ができた。
rows.en: I shoved harder, and turbulence sprang up right in front of me.

ghs.en: Pushing into it with strength, turbulence was created in front of my eyes.

rows.jp: 風の通り道。

ghs.en: In the path of the wind.

rows.jp: 耳鳴り。

ghs.en: Buzzing in my ears.

rows.jp: それと、先輩。

ghs.en: And then, Senpai.

rows.jp: 「おはようございます」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Good morning."

rows.jp: 「あら、おはようございます」

ghs.en: Misato: "Dear me, good morning."

rows.jp: 「どうですか、アンテナ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "How is the antenna doing?"

rows.jp: 「ぼちぼち、というところですか」

ghs.en: Misato: "It is coming along little by little, I could say."

rows.jp: 「これって、次の日曜日が予定日だったんですよね」
rows.en: “The antenna was scheduled for next Sunday, wasn't it?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And, the scheduled completion date is next Sunday, right."

rows.jp: 「……よく記憶してますね」

ghs.en: Misato: "...you remembered that so well!"

rows.jp: 「一応は」

ghs.en: Taichi: "In a sense I do."

rows.jp: 「そうです。何も起こらなければ、ここは……」
rows.en: “Yes. If nothing had happened, this place...”

ghs.en: Misato: "Right then. If nothing goes wrong, because us being here..."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese begins a conditional statement that if nothing had happened, this place or project would have proceeded. The English inserts 'because,' uses an object pronoun as a subject, and fails to convey the clause.
ghs.remedy: Yes. If nothing had happened, this place would have...

highlights.text: If nothing goes wrong, because us being here...

rows.jp: 「でも、人が亡くなったんですから、仕方ありません……あ、ごめんなさい」
rows.en: “But someone died, so there was nothing we could do... Oh, I'm sorry.”

ghs.en: Misato: "But because of that human death, there is nothing that could be done... ah, apologies!"

rows.jp: 「いえー」

ghs.en: Taichi: "'Tis nooothing."

rows.jp: 本当に謝る必要なんてない。
rows.en: She really had nothing to apologize for.

ghs.en: There's really no need for her to apologize,

rows.jp: 傷ついてさえいないのだから、俺は。

ghs.en: because I don't hurt in the slightest, I don't.

rows.jp: 「まあ、そのせいで屋上に行くのが禁止になったわけですから」
rows.en: “Well, that's why they put the roof off-limits.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, because of 'that' coming to the rooftop had become forbidden."
ghs.assessment: The adverbial phrase is incorrectly made the subject of 'had become,' leaving the causal sentence malformed.
ghs.remedy: because of that, going to the rooftop had been forbidden

highlights.text: because of 'that' coming to the rooftop had become forbidden

rows.jp: 「……あなた方はけっこう勝手に来てたようですけどね」
rows.en: “...Though you and the others came up whenever you felt like it.”

ghs.en: Misato: "...but all of you people seem to just show up like you please."

rows.jp: 「それを言ったら、今の先輩だって」
rows.en: “You could say the same about yourself right now.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If you have to put it like that, what about you right now, Senpai."

rows.jp: 見合わされた二人の顔。同時に頬が緩む。
rows.en: Our eyes met, and we both smiled at once.

ghs.en: The faces of us both meet and exchange glances. And simultaneously, our cheeks relax.

rows.jp: 「じゃ、二人とも停学です。イエロー停学」

ghs.en: Misato: "Then we will both be suspended. Yellow suspension."

rows.jp: 「そりゃ厳しいや」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Awww, that's so strict."

rows.jp: 「……これって、先輩が一人でここまで？」
rows.en: “...Did you really build all this by yourself?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...this thing, have you gotten it this far alone, Senpai?"

rows.jp: 「図面があったので、なんとか」
rows.en: “I had the blueprints, so I managed.”

ghs.en: Misato: "There were blueprints, so yes, somehow."

rows.jp: 「でも、大変でした。いったんバラバラにされてましたから」
rows.en: “It was hard, though. The whole thing had been taken apart.”

ghs.en: Misato: "But it was so much trouble. Because it had been all broken up at one time."

rows.jp: それでも先輩は、誰にも助けを求めなかった。
rows.en: Even so, Misato hadn't asked anyone for help.

ghs.en: And despite this, Senpai did not seek the help of anyone else.

rows.jp: 仮借ない陽光に身をさらして、一人で、部活を続けていた。
rows.en: Under the merciless sun, she'd kept the club going all by herself.

ghs.en: She exposed herself to the merciless sunlight, alone, and continued her club activities.

rows.jp: 「……今さら手伝いましょうかってのも、虫の良い話なんでしょうね」
rows.en: “...I guess offering to help now would be pretty self-serving.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...even if I said wanted to help after all, that would be simply selfishness talking, would it."
ghs.assessment: The subordinate clause omits the subject before 'wanted.'
ghs.remedy: if I said I wanted to help

highlights.text: if I said wanted to help

rows.jp: 先輩は相好を崩す。

ghs.en: Senpai collapses into a big smile.

rows.jp: 「ありがとうです」

ghs.en: Misato: "Thank you so much."

rows.jp: 「お気持ちだけで十分ですよ」

ghs.en: Misato: "Your best wishes alone are enough!"

rows.jp: まあ、こんなものか。
rows.en: Well. That was about what I'd expected.

ghs.en: Well, that's what it'll be then.

rows.jp: 「いつだって、使ってくれて良かったのに」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Regardless, I would have been glad to be of use to you, anywhere and at any time."

rows.jp: あなたの逃避に利用してくれて。

ghs.en: Make use of me in your escape.
ghs.assessment: This is the narrator's continuation that she could always have used him to facilitate her escape. The English turns it into a present imperative addressed aloud.
ghs.remedy: You could have used me as part of your escape.

highlights.text: Make use of me in your escape.

rows.jp: 「あっ、いいんですいいんです、平気ですから」

ghs.en: Misato: "Ah, all good I am all good, I will be alright."

rows.jp: 「そのかわりといってはなんですけど、今度またゆっくりお茶しましょう」
rows.en: “It's not much in return, but let's have tea together again sometime.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Instead of that, however, I would much rather for us to have a quiet tea break together next time."

rows.jp: 「はい」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yes!"
